goal: Add two-pass [[package]] rule specificity ordering (prefixed beats bare), a cross-ecosystem ambiguity warning diagnostic, and the BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems DiagnosticCode variant.
architecture: Five sequential tasks ordered by compile-time dependency. T1 adds the new DiagnosticCode variant so downstream crates compile. T2 fixes the specificity ordering in walk.rs (two-pass find, no new types required). T3a adds the cross-ecosystem diagnostic pass (requires T1 for the variant) and its positive test using a napi-style fixture — a single directory with both Cargo.toml and package.json named 'my-pkg', which produces one packages-map entry with two canonical ManifestDecls and triggers the diagnostic. T3b adds the negative-case regression tests (no new implementation). T4 adds the §G.13 docs row. The packages map keys are always PackageId::Bare (IgnoreWalkLocator builds ids via PackageId::parse(name) on raw manifest names); ecosystem information for AC-5 is sourced exclusively from pkg.manifests canonical ManifestDecl entries, never from map keys.
tech_stack: cargo test integration tests in crates/callisto-graph/tests/

tasks.commit_message:
fix(graph): two-pass [[package]] lookup — prefixed rules win over bare rules

Before: cfg.packages.iter().find() used first-match-wins across all rule
types, so a bare rule declared before a prefixed rule would incorrectly win.
After: pass 1 finds the first Prefixed match; bare rules are only
considered when no Prefixed rule matches. Implements SPEC-002 AC-1/1b/2/3/4a/4b (with AC-3 first-prefixed-wins test).

tasks.commit_message:
docs: add BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems row to §G.13 diagnostic registry table

Appends the row per SPEC-002 AC-11: Code=BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems,
Emitted-by=§G.4 walk, escalated_by=—, governed_by=— (advisory warning).

reasoning:
Decomposition logic:

Task ordering is dictated by compile-time dependencies:
- T1 must come first. T3a's test file references DiagnosticCode::BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems. Until T1 lands, the test file does not compile. T2 does not reference the new variant so it could run concurrently with T1; placed second for clean serialization of the TDD cycle.
- T2 has no runtime dependency on T1 or T3a. It touches only walk.rs (specificity) and per_package_config_test.rs. Placed before T3a so the walk.rs baseline is correct before the diagnostic pass is added.
- T3a depends on T1 (DiagnosticCode variant) and modifies walk.rs (same file as T2). Separated from T2 so each has its own red-green TDD cycle and distinct commit.
- T3b depends on T3a (needs T3a's test file to exist and T3a's implementation to be correct). These are negative-case regression tests. Their red phase is: before T3a the entire test file in T3b would pass vacuously (no diagnostics at all), but after T3a any false positive is caught. The 'no new implementation' note means no walk.rs changes in T3b.
- T4 depends on T1 (the variant name must exist before we add it to docs) but is otherwise independent. Placed last as a pure docs edit.

Critical correctness fact for T3a diagnostic pass:
Packages map keys (the BTreeMap<PackageId, Package> built in walk.rs) are ALWAYS PackageId::Bare. IgnoreWalkLocator builds ids via PackageId::parse(name).unwrap_or_else(|_| PackageId::Bare(name)) from the raw manifest name string. A plain package name like 'my-pkg' parses as Bare. Therefore key.ecosystem() is always None — calling it to compute the distinct-ecosystem set would produce an empty BTreeSet and the diagnostic would never fire. The correct approach is to call pkg.manifests.iter().filter(canonical).map(d.ecosystem()) to collect ecosystems from the ManifestDecl entries. ManifestDecl::ecosystem() delegates to ManifestFormat::ecosystem() and returns Ecosystem directly (not Option<Ecosystem>), so no unwrap is needed.

Critical correctness fact for T3a fixture:
The AC-5 trigger is a SINGLE directory containing both Cargo.toml and package.json with the same package name (the napi case). IgnoreWalkLocator groups both manifests into the same by_path entry (same directory path), so walk.rs builds one Package with two canonical ManifestDecls. Two DIFFERENT directories containing packages with the same bare name (e.g. crates/foo for Cargo and packages/foo for npm, both named 'foo') would both produce primary_id = PackageId::Bare('foo') and the second package_manifest_decls.insert call would trigger GraphError::DuplicatePackage, causing Workspace::load to return Err before the diagnostic pass is reached. That case is therefore not a valid AC-5 fixture.

AC-10 placement:
The prompt's task ordering lists T4 as 'AC-10 serde test + AC-11 docs row.' However, the serde test for BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems cannot meaningfully be separated from the variant addition: writing the test before the variant gives a compile error (which IS the red phase) and adding the variant makes the test pass (green). Keeping both in T1 produces one clean TDD cycle for the variant addition. T4 therefore contains only the AC-11 docs row; AC-10 coverage is in T1.

Two-pass specificity implementation choice (T2):
Two separate iter().find() calls rather than a single pass with priority scoring. This is simpler to read, matches the spec's described algorithm exactly, and avoids any helper struct. The first pass finds the first Prefixed match (pattern.ecosystem().is_some()). If it returns None (no Prefixed rule matches), the second pass finds the first overall match (necessarily Bare at that point, since all Prefixed rules failed). The or_else closure is only evaluated when the first find returns None, so there is no double-scan in the common case where a Prefixed rule matches early.

no unwrap() in library code:
The diagnostic pass uses ManifestDecl::ecosystem() which returns Ecosystem directly. The eco_list construction uses ecosystems.iter().next().map(|e| e.prefix()).unwrap_or('cargo') for the example prefix in the message — this is safe because this branch is only reached when ecosystems.len() >= 2, so iter().next() will never return None. The unwrap_or is a belt-and-suspenders fallback that satisfies the no-unwrap lint in library code.

T4 anchor for docs row insertion:
The ChangesetsConfigKeyDropped row is used as the text anchor for insertion. The spec table is in §G.13 and currently ends at that row. The new BareRuleMatchesMultipleEcosystems row is appended after it. Line numbers are not used as anchors per the spec requirement.
